questions.question: A MemoryBackend subclass that narrows CAPABILITIES (a ClassVar) no longer gates anything on the kernel, because capabilities now come from the driver. Master honoured it. How should this PR handle it?

options.label: Restore it (Recommended)
options.description: MemoryBackend.__init__ builds its driver with type(self).CAPABILITIES, so a subclass's narrower set gates the Store again, as on master. The driver gets a `capabilities=` constructor argument. A subclass that claims more than the driver backs (e.g. GLOB) is refused at construction rather than failing at call time. A test seen failing first pins it.

options.label: Document it only
options.description: Keep the kernel behaviour (the driver's set decides) and add a migration bullet: override the `capabilities` property, not the CAPABILITIES ClassVar. Smaller change, but a silent behaviour regression for anyone narrowing a test double.

questions.question: Spec 003 BE-030 says reconciling BackendContract.dfy's Write with WR-010's gate order is 're-homed to BK-434', but BK-434 is about RFC-0021 encodings and never mentions it. Where should that obligation live?

options.label: New backlog item (Recommended)
options.description: File a new BK item (S, formal) for the Write/WR-010 departure, with spec BE-030 and WR-010. Point BE-030 and the bk-389 dossier at it. It does not fit BK-434's encoding scope, since the departure exists on both namespaces.

options.label: Fold into BK-434
options.description: Create a BK-434 dossier recording the WR-010/Write reconciliation, add BE-030 and WR-010 to its spec field, and fix the bk-389 dossier sentences. No new ID, but it widens an item whose open decision is about encodings.

questions.question: Out of scope, measured on both revisions: writing a bytearray or memoryview to either Memory class fails (the driver short-circuits only bytes). On the PR the error is wrapped as RemoteStoreError instead of a raw AttributeError or TypeError. File it?

options.label: File a BUG item (Recommended)
options.description: New BUG item: Memory drivers reject bytearray and memoryview content although the kernel's own guard and feed accept them. Not fixed in this PR, since WritableContent types it as bytes | BinaryIO.

options.label: Don't file
options.description: Treat it as out of contract (WritableContent excludes bytearray) and drop it, mentioning it only in the close report.
